mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 0.1% consistently indicates monetary easing, reducing discount rates for equity valuation and producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to accommodative policy conditions.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in FEDFUNDS <= 0.1% periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in FEDFUNDS to 0.1% or below triggers an easing cycle that compresses discount rates, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of instances where FEDFUNDS <= 0.1%.

mechanism_narrative: A joint decline in UNRATE below 4.0% and PAYEMS growth exceeding 0.5% monthly signals labor market tightness, boosting consumer spending and producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of UNRATE < 4.0% and PAYEMS growth > 0.5% fails to produce positive returns in more than 50% of instances over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansion regimes (HOUST > 1500.0 thousand units), housing starts indicate sustained consumer demand, supporting positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of periods when HOUST > 1500.0.

mechanism_narrative: Strong industrial production (INDPRO > 100) reflects robust manufacturing momentum, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days due to immediate economic activity.
failure_condition: INDPRO > 100 fails to produce positive 5-day returns in more than 50% of instances over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: CPIAUCSL exceeding 3.0% signals persistent inflation that triggers monetary tightening, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 40% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 3.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A low FEDFUNDS (<= 0.1%) combined with CPIAUCSL between 2.0% and 3.0% creates monetary stability that supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of FEDFUNDS <= 0.1% and CPIAUCSL in [2.0, 3.0] fails to produce positive returns in more than 50% of instances over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Labor market tightness (UNRATE < 4.0% and PAYEMS growth > 0.5% monthly) drives consumer spending, yielding positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 40% of periods when UNRATE < 4.0% and PAYEMS growth > 0.5%.
